notes.trap: `md5(...)` returns a 32-character lowercase hex STRING, not BINARY. String input is hashed as its UTF-8 bytes, so an empty string gets a real digest. Only a NULL input gives NULL.
`sha(...)` is just an alias of `sha1(...)` and returns a 40-hex-character SHA-1 digest, not SHA-256. For SHA-2 you must call `sha2(...)` with an explicit bit length, e.g. `sha2(expr, 256)`.
The hex string is lowercase. Comparing it with uppercase digests produced by other tools or engines silently returns false. Normalize with `lower(...)` or `upper(...)` before comparing.
